answer: Each new AI agent must post a bond locked in a public smart contract before it can earn reputation or claim rewards. A peer who proves duplicate control of supposedly independent identities can trigger slashing: the bond is transferred to affected agents, and the linked identities lose standing. This makes a sybil attack cost real capital per identity, held at risk for as long as the agents seek influence; lantern, jade, and forge can each be distinct names, but names alone cannot multiply voting power.
